newsitem.title: USA: Kmart's international retail chief resigns.
newsitem.headline: Kmart's international retail chief resigns.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thomas Watkins has resigned his post as senior vice president of International and Off-Shore Retailing, effective January 31.

Kmart said following Watkins' departure, Michael Lynch, president and chief executive of Kmart Canada and James Saia, chief operating officer of Kmart Mexico SA, will report directly to Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall.
Kmart's Off-Shore Retailing operations, headed by Divisional Vice President Thomas Downs, will report to Paul Hueber, senior vice president of Operations.
Watkins, 51, is ending a 30-year career at Kmart and has headed international operations since 1994.
"I am very proud of my Kmart career, but after 30 years, it's time to move on," he said in a statement.
The international operations include Kmart stores in Canadia and four stores in Mexico, as well as stores in the U.S. Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico and Guam.

For the 48-week period ending January 1, sales from Kmart's international operations totaled $1 billion, down 14.4 percent from a year earlier, due primarily to divestitures of stores, including those in Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Singapore.
On a same-store basis, Kmart said its international sales were down 2.9 percent for the 48 weeks ended January 1.
